div.ab: ⁊ gemet, swylce man on Wintancestre healde.
⁊ gange án gemet ⁊ án gewihte, swylce mon on Lundenbyrig ⁊ on Wintanceastre healde.
⁊ gange án gemet ⁊ an gewihte, swilce man on Lundenbirig ⁊ on Wintaceastre healde.
⁊ gange an gemet ⁊ án gewihte, swylce mon on Lundenbyrig ⁊ on Wintanceastre healde.
et mensura, sicut apud Wincestram habetur.
⁊ gange án gemet ⁊ an gewihte, swilce man on Lundenbirig ⁊ on Wintaceastre healde.
And gange an gemet and an gewihte swylce man on Lundenbyrig and on Wintanceastre healde.
und (es gehe Ein A D G2) Maass (und Ein Gewicht A D G2), solches wie (in London und A D G2) in Winchester gehalten wird.
and (let there be one, A D G2) measure (and one weight, A D G2), such as is kept (in London and, A D G2) in Winchester.
And there shall be one system of measurement, and one standard of weights, such as is in use in London and in Winchester.
and the system of measurement, as is observed in Winchester.
And there is to be one standard of weights and one standard of measures, just as is used in London and Winchester.

note.seg: Von dem Mehr der Rec. II halt ich die Worte über London sicher, und daher die anderen mit Wahrscheinlichkeit, für späteren Zusatz, vielleicht noch 10. Jhs.—Vgl. Gl Mass 6; Gewicht 7—8a.—Dass das offene Land anders regiert ward als die Stadt, folgert hieraus Gomme Making of London 91 mit Unrecht. Das Normalmass gab sie allein

Of the additional matter in Rec. II, I hold the words about London certainly, and therefore the others probably, to be a later addition, perhaps still of the 10th cent. — Cf. Gl Mass 6; Gewicht 7—8a. — Gomme, Making of London 91, wrongly infers from this that the open country was governed differently from the town. It alone supplied the standard measure

Von dem Mehr der Rec. II halt ich die Worte über London sicher, und daher die anderen mit Wahrscheinlichkeit, für späteren Zusatz, vielleicht noch 10. Jhs.—Vgl. Gl Mass 6; Gewicht 7—8a.—Dass das offene Land anders regiert ward als die Stadt, folgert hieraus Gomme Making of London 91 mit Unrecht. Das Normalmass gab sie allein

Of the additional matter in Rec. II, I hold the words about London certainly, and therefore the others probably, to be a later addition, perhaps still of the 10th cent. — Cf. Gl Mass 6; Gewicht 7—8a. — Gomme, Making of London 91, wrongly infers from this that the open country was governed differently from the town. It alone supplied the standard measure
Vgl. Gl London 29b; über Winchesters Mass s. Kitchin Charter of St. Giles’ fair a. 1349 p. 9
Cf. Gl London 29b; on the Winchester measure see Kitchin Charter of St. Giles’ fair a. 1349 p. 9

The reference may be to measures of capacity, a subject on which unfortunately we have very little definite information for the Saxon period. For notes on the amber and the sester see Harmer, Historical Documents, pp. 73, 79 f.

Liebermann suggests that this standard of weight may have been identical with the later ‘husting weight’ (see Sharpe, London and the Kingdom, i. p. 10) and this again may have been meant by the publicum pondus of the tenth and eleventh centuries (see Napier and Stevenson, Crawford Charters, pp. 77–8).

Towards the end of the tenth century London was becoming far more important than Winchester, hence the precedence given it in the later recension of this regulation represented by A, D, G₂. Winchester, noted for its cloth manufacture which dated from very early times, and for its trade in wines, remained a prosperous commercial centre, however, till the thirteenth century. For a short sketch of its history see Kitchin, Charter of St Giles’s Fair, a.d. 1349, pp. 8–12.

note.label: Winchester
note.seg: Quadripartitus supports the text as above, but the Wulfstan MSS expand to: “And one standard of measurement and one standard of weight is to be current, as is observed in London and in Winchester.”
